digest.intro: AI power shifts, a dormant stem cell reserve, and a machined boiler.

items.title: Jensen Huang Out at Nvidia
items.blurb: Nvidia's co-founder and 30-year CEO forced out after an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore firm suspected of routing sanctioned chips to China — espionage, sex scandal, and AI supply-chain politics knotted together. CFO Colette Kress takes the interim role. Singapore separately says the US was uncooperative in its own probe, which is its own geopolitical tell.

items.title: Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow; Ukraine Prisoner Swap Agreed
items.blurb: US envoys met Putin in Moscow today while a Ukraine-Russia prisoner exchange was agreed in Abu Dhabi — the diplomacy track is moving faster than most expected. Europe is loudly insisting it cannot be cut out of any security settlement, and the schism between Brussels and Washington is sharpening into something structural rather than rhetorical.

items.title: Hormuz Down to 30 Ships a Day
items.blurb: The Strait of Hormuz is running at roughly 22% of its normal throughput — 30 escorted transits a day against a 138-vessel baseline — after a Saudi tanker was attacked November 11. Qatar is reportedly negotiating a narrow two-week window to forestall US strikes on Iran, with APEC on November 18-19 as the hard deadline everyone is quietly watching.

items.title: Anthropic's IPO Numbers, Actually Read
items.blurb: Willison transcribed the roadshow video and the most interesting detail is operational: Anthropic now trains and serves Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs, and AMD GPUs — a multi-chip bet most people thought wasn't worth the engineering cost. The payoff: when they onboarded AMD this year, Claude itself ported nearly 100% of the kernels in three days with almost no human intervention, a task that previously took dozens of engineers months.

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's Execution Engine
items.blurb: Google's new Hydrogen model is explicitly designed as the fast, cheap half of a two-model stack — Carbon and Argon for hard reasoning, Hydrogen for rapid execution in agentic loops. At $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens flat across a 1M-token context window, the pricing is a direct signal that Google is subsidizing market share in the agentic workflow layer, timed precisely to land during Anthropic's roadshow week.

items.title: Technology as a Search Problem
items.blurb: Brian Potter frames invention not as inspiration but as navigation through an incomprehensibly vast design space — every conceivable arrangement of parts, materials, and phenomena — where the core problem is that you can't see most of the space from where you stand. He traces why some domains advance fast (dense, legible feedback; well-mapped adjacencies) and others stall for generations, which reframes why Bell Labs worked and why most R&D doesn't.

items.title: Machining a Whole Boiler Because Why Not
items.blurb: Hans Gaensbauer set out to repair a Gaggia Classic Pro and ended up milling an entirely new boiler and group head from stainless steel stock — which meant reverse-engineering a cast part never intended for machining, including the portafilter locking contours and the perforated distribution plate. The piece is a clean reminder that the gap between 'repair' and 'remake from scratch' is mostly a question of how far down the rabbit hole you're willing to go.

items.title: A Hidden Reserve of Blood Stem Cells
items.blurb: German Cancer Research Center identified a population of deeply dormant hematopoietic stem cells in mice that respond far more cautiously to inflammatory signals than the conventional HSC pool — suggesting the body keeps a guarded reserve that conventional stem cell counts miss entirely. Mouse-only and early, but structurally interesting: if the same population exists in humans, it reframes how we think about lifetime blood system resilience and what depletes first under stress or aging.
